messages:
lee: Heads-up from quarterly access scan: ~18 unexpected grants to prod KMS key in last 48h.
anita: uhh. service or human principals?
sam: pulling grant list now, give me a minute.
ops-bot: deploy-notice: key-manager service rolled canary config (enable_auto_approve=true) at 2026-03-20T11:02Z
sam: most grants issued to serviceAccount:key-manager@redwood.iam and three direct user principals (jordan, renee, tom).
lee: this smells like the new auto-approve path. Treat as privileged escalation incident.
anita: immediate actions: 1) disable auto-approve in canary 2) revoke all user grants 3) snapshot grants and policies 4) assess need to rotate key.
sam: revoke commands queued — doing user revokes first: `gcloud kms grants list --key=projects/redwood/locations/us-west1/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/primary` then revoke with grant ids.
anita: hold on rotation until we know what services depend on those svcacct grants. rotating will break things.
lee: agree. sam, capture outputs and attach to INC-5621. also enable strict alerting: new KMS grants > 2/hr.
audit-bot: export complete: gs://redwood-audit/kms/2026-03-20/grants.csv attached to INC-5621
sam: user revokes completed for jordan and renee. tom revoke returned PERMISSION_DENIED — looks like tom has org-level binding.
anita: open follow-up to infra team to remove tom's binding. tag infra-oncall.
lee: patch RBAC: disallow direct user bindings to roles/cloudkms.admin; force bindings through groups or service accounts.
anita: I'll draft a short PR with conditional bindings and a temporary deny rule for direct users.
sam: can we add a runbook checkpoint: any feature flag that grants >1 admin entitlement in a day requires two approvers and a 24h canary window.
lee: good. schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow 09:30 to confirm root cause and next steps (recert cycle, alert tuning, RBAC patch).
anita: posting runbook link in INC-5621: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-surge
lee: monitoring enabled. watch window 24h. closing thread, will update ticket with PM invite.
